title: Find Minimum Time to Reach Last Room I
summary: In a dungeon grid with n x m rooms, each room (i, j) becomes accessible after moveTime[i][j] seconds.
statement: In a dungeon grid with n x m rooms, each room (i, j) becomes accessible after moveTime[i][j] seconds. Starting from room (0, 0) at time t = 0, you need to find the minimum time required to reach room (n - 1, m - 1) by moving to adjacent rooms, where each move between adjacent rooms takes exactly one second.
constraints: move_time is a 2–50 by 2–50 nonnegative matrix.
Start at (0,0) at time zero; before entering a neighbor, wait until its opening time, then spend one second moving.
Return the earliest arrival at the bottom-right room using four-directional moves.
hints: Reaching a room earlier can never hurt because waiting is allowed.
Use Dijkstra with arrival time as distance and a time-dependent but monotone edge relaxation.
For each neighbor compute max(current time, neighbor opens)+1 and relax it in a heap.
The relaxation has the FIFO property, so the first finalized destination time is globally minimal.
editorial: The relaxation has the FIFO property, so the first finalized destination time is globally minimal.

tests.explanation: Wait until time four, then two one-second moves arrive at time six.
With no waiting, the shortest three-edge route takes three seconds.
